chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Abdullah ibn Al-Salt, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the young girl whose father marries her off: does she have authority (to choose) when she reaches adulthood? He (peace be upon him) said: No, she does not have authority with her father.

He said, And I asked him about the virgin when she reaches the maturity of women: does she have authority with her father? He (peace be upon him) said: No, she does not have authority with her father as long as she has not grown up (reached full maturity).

key_terms.تَكْبَرْ: to grow up / reach full maturity

ai.seo_question: Does a father have the right to marry off his unmarried daughter without her consent in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the distinction is drawn between physical maturity (bulugh) and full independent maturity (kibr), clarifying that a virgin daughter remains under her father's guardianship (wilayah) until she reaches the latter stage. This establishes the Shia juristic view that while the father has the right to contract the marriage, the daughter's consent is not strictly required for validity during this intermediate phase, distinguishing it from the 'thayyibah' (previously married woman) who has full autonomy. The hadith underscores the paternal role in preserving social and familial interests during the daughter's transition to full legal capacity.
